purpose: Check the analytic-vector criterion used in the finite-qubit block limit, without changing its frozen primary note.

source.author: Barry Simon
source.title: Topics in Functional Analysis
source.read_boundary: Title page and complete PDF pages 9-10, printed pages 24-25: definition, Nussbaum lemma, Theorem 1.7 and its proof. No full-book read claimed.
source.criterion_paraphrase: A symmetric operator whose domain contains a dense set of analytic vectors is essentially self-adjoint.
source.attribution: Simon's text attributes the theorem to Nelson (1959) and gives a proof patterned after Nussbaum. The original Nelson paper itself was not obtained.

hypotheses.symmetric: The finite real quadratic sum of Hermitian squares is symmetric and positive on the finite-particle Fock core.
hypotheses.dense_domain: Finite linear combinations of occupation vectors are dense in the Fock space for the fixed finite number of modes.
hypotheses.invariant_domain: Each quadratic factor changes occupation by at most two, so every power acts on the finite-particle core.
hypotheses.analytic_bound: For initial maximum occupation m, each successive quadratic action costs at most C(m+2j+1). The product is bounded by C_m C_0^n (n+m+1)!, making the power series with denominator n! converge for a sufficiently small positive parameter.

limits: This receipt checks only the self-adjointness criterion. The weighted-number estimates, Duhamel bound and claimed physical scope require their separate derivation and independent review. The PDF remains outside the repository.
